title: OWASP MCP Top 10 and the MCP Server Security Standard
summary: John Van Lowe gives two lightning talks on MCP security: the OWASP Top 10 and the MSSS.
learn: The OWASP MCP Top 10 covers risks where MCP lets LLMs reach data sources and tools, often with no human in the loop: prompt injection, insufficient authentication, shadow MCP servers, context injection, secret exposure and tool poisoning.
He walks a recent supply-chain compromise through those risks, from a package upgrade to command execution, exfiltration and token mismanagement.
The MCP Server Security Standard (MSSS) has eight domains and compliance levels from essential to maximum assurance, and he suggests developers meet at least the six essential controls.

Controls map to threats: secret redaction, OAuth delegation, least privilege and RBAC, URL validation against server-side request forgery, container hardening, audit logging and file system sandboxing.
He frames this against PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001 and FedRAMP, and points to VetSec, OWASP Austin and other groups for getting involved.
